edit.description: The reserved set gets one home beside `ENGINE_KEY` (:3178): a new `DECLARATION_TABLE` const replacing the six bare `"declaration"` literals (:3201, :3256, :3408, :3487, :4599, :4715), and a new `pub(crate) RESERVED_LOCK_ROOT_KEYS` naming both. The corruption is here: `write_rollup` (:587) writes the stamp, then `doc[kind.as_str()]` per rollup (:598), then `Declarations::write_into` (:4553) assigns `doc["declaration"]` (:4599) over whatever sits there — so a kind named `engine` erases the stamp and a kind named `declaration` loses its whole rollup array, both silently. A unit test derives the set from the real writer rather than hand-listing it (`engineering.md`, "A seam gate reads what the real writer wrote"): `write_rollup` over an empty rollup map, re-parsed, carries exactly these root keys.

New `RESERVED_LOCK_KEY_RULE` (`kind.reserved-lock-key`) beside `GOVERNS_COLLISION_RULE` (:594) and `COLLECTION_ADDRESS_COLLISION_RULE` (:600), and `reserved_kind_name_diagnostics` beside `governs_collision_diagnostics` (:621) and `collection_address_collision_diagnostics` (:685) — the fourth member of that family, same shape: one error per kind fact whose name is in `drift::RESERVED_LOCK_ROOT_KEYS`, naming the key, what the lock uses it for, and the one exit (rename the kind). A unit test beside `a_kind_collision_names_the_fact_that_diverges_from_the_builtin` (:908).

Wire the refusal at the dispatch site its three siblings already share — `kind_collision_diagnostics` (:296), `governs_collision_diagnostics` (:303), `collection_address_collision_diagnostics` (:311) — over the same effective kind set, so a committed lock carrying such a kind is refused at the one door every read verb passes through.

The integration cases: a `Declarations` carrying a `KindFactRow` named `declaration`, and one named `engine`, each draw the `kind.reserved-lock-key` error from `check`, and a kind named anything else draws none. The hand-built-row pattern is the file's own; `tests/it/coverage.rs` holds the governs-collision sibling's cases and stays untouched.

summary: A kind named for a reserved lock root key — `engine` or `declaration` — is refused loud instead of silently erasing the stamp or losing its whole rollup.

tests.asserts: a kind fact named `declaration` or `engine` draws the `kind.reserved-lock-key` error naming the key and the rename remedy; any other kind name draws none
the reserved root-key set equals the root keys a real `write_rollup` writes outside the per-kind rollup loop, so a future root key joins the set by construction

acceptance: cargo test green, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean, cargo fmt --all --check clean, and the drift.rs pin failing if a root key is added to the lock without joining the reserved set.
notes: Named but not taken in ce916185's body as a pre-existing shape question the engine stamp joined. Rejected: an SDK-side pre-emption at kind definition — all three sibling collision refusals live at the gate over the effective kind set, and emit rewrites the lock whole every run, so a second home buys nothing. Rejected: re-namespacing the rollups under a reserved table — a lock-format break every committed lock pays. scoped at 039eb92b
